accuracy.evidence: Homologous series features match AQA 8462 4.7.1 and BBC Bitesize: same general formula, successive members differ by CH2, same functional group so similar reactions, and a gradual trend in physical properties. Rules shown are CnH2n+2, CnH2n, CnH2n+1OH and CnH2nO2 for the acids. Boiling points in the chart use standard data values: methane −162, ethane −89, propane −42, butane −1, pentane 36 °C; methanol 65, ethanol 78, propanol 97, butanol 118, pentanol 138 °C.

misconceptions.evidence: Addresses the slips learners make with series: thinking members differ by CH3 instead of CH2, counting only the extra carbon and forgetting the two hydrogens, grouping molecules by carbon count (ethane with ethanol) instead of functional group, assuming 'same family' means identical boiling points, and writing C4H10OH by dropping the alkane formula onto an alcohol.

lab_distinct.evidence: A family wall plus a boiling-point chart: the learner opens the gaps between rows to reveal +CH2, taps a column header to test that family's general formula on every member, sorts tray molecules into columns by functional group, then drags a guess marker on a property chart. None of the existing labs pairs a cross-family comparison wall with a trend graph; the closest is the alkane chain builder (flag_alkane) at a low shingle overlap.

lab_teaches.evidence: Opening the alcohol gaps one at a time makes the constant +CH2 step visible before it is named; testing the rule shows each family has one formula that fits all its members; sorting C2H6 versus C2H5OH forces the functional-group criterion; the alkane chart shows +73, +47, +41, +37 rises so the learner guesses pentane from the trend, and the alcohol chart shows similar reactions but different boiling points.

predictions.evidence: Five locked-in predictions with tempting distractors the lab then tests: 'One extra CH3' for propanol versus ethanol, 'C4H10OH' for butanol, 'Yes: same number of carbons' for ethane and ethanol, 'It is the same: same family' for the boiling point of pentane, and 'Yes: same family, same properties' for butanol versus propanol.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Checked in the browser on desktop and iPhone 13: choosing an extra CH3 gets feedback that the chain grows by one CH2 unit; adding only a carbon is told the two hydrogens come too; picking a molecule with matching carbons but a different group is told series are set by the functional group; multi-step slips get the count of CH2 units between the members; the correct member is then shown on the wall.

readability.evidence: Flesch-Kincaid grade 4.9 for kid text and 8.8 for adult text, inside the 6.5 and 9.5 limits; kid paragraphs use the picture of a family that grows by the same small piece each time and give one worked step from ethanol to propanol, while adult paragraphs define each feature of a series in a short sentence.

no_filler.evidence: The filler regex passes and the explanation overlap check is under the 12% limit; each adult paragraph has one job (the CH2 step, general formulae, the functional group deciding the family, the physical trend and the named mistakes); lab messages are built from the live molecule, its formula and the measured boiling-point change, not from repeated stock text.

mobile.evidence: The phone sweep on iPhone 13 and a 360x640 Android viewport in both themes reports 0 findings; screenshots of the four-column wall, the alkane and alcohol charts and the challenge show formulas readable at 390 px, value labels set clear of the y-axis ticks and difference badges, and the down/up 10 °C and Check my guess buttons wrapping without clipping.

accessibility.evidence: axe-core WCAG 2.1 AA reports no violations in light and dark themes on desktop and phone; the canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the open gaps, the family rule being tested, or the current boiling-point guess; buttons for Open next gap, the family rules, the sort choices and the 10 °C nudges do everything the taps and drag do.
